/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Builders
  Scenarios for witnesses and tests: a scene and a trace from a few named quantities, padding by
  timestamp, masking under a manifest, and the `Scenario` a witness file declares.

  A witness must be indistinguishable from adapter output to an atom, so everything here goes
  through the `World` constructors and nothing else. Reachable from `Witness/**` and `Tests/**`
  only: a rule that could build its own evidence proves nothing.

  No default magnitude lives here — every extent, speed and distance is an argument the witness
  writes through a `Units` constructor.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Monitor

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Build

/-- Cardinal unit headings in the world frame (+x east, +y north). -/
def east : Vec := (Q.ofInt 1, Q.zero)
def west : Vec := (Q.ofInt (-1), Q.zero)
def north : Vec := (Q.zero, Q.ofInt 1)
def south : Vec := (Q.zero, Q.ofInt (-1))

def scale (h : Vec) (k : Q) : Vec := (Q.mul h.1 k, Q.mul h.2 k)

/-- A road user with position, heading and speed; velocity follows the heading, path length
    is the caller's (cumulative) figure, extents are half-length/half-width/half-height. -/
def user (track : TrackId) (classes : List RoadUserClass) (pos : Vec) (heading : Vec) (speed : Q)
    (halfExtent : Q × Q × Q) (pathLength : Option Q := none) : RoadUser :=
  { track := track
    classes := some classes
    kin := { position := some pos
             heading := some heading
             velocity := some (scale heading speed)
             speed := some speed
             extent := some halfExtent
             pathLength := pathLength } }

/-- A road user of which only the position (and classes) was observed. -/
def sparseUser (track : TrackId) (classes : List RoadUserClass) (pos : Vec) : RoadUser :=
  { track := track, classes := some classes, kin := { position := some pos } }

def withSignals (u : RoadUser) (f : Signals → Signals) : RoadUser := { u with sig := f u.sig }
def withKin (u : RoadUser) (f : Kin → Kin) : RoadUser := { u with kin := f u.kin }
/-- A measured relation from `a` to `b`, with the measured fields the source supplies. -/
def relation (a b : TrackId) (f : MeasuredRelation → MeasuredRelation := id) : MeasuredRelation := f { a := a, b := b }
def withRelations (s : Scene) (rs : List MeasuredRelation) : Scene := { s with relations := rs }

/-- A region of a kind with a polygon boundary. -/
def region (id : RegionId) (kind : StructureKind) (boundary : List Vec) : Structure :=
  { id := id, kind := kind, boundary := some boundary }
/-- An axis-aligned rectangular region from two corners. -/
def rect (id : RegionId) (kind : StructureKind) (x0 y0 x1 y1 : Q) : Structure :=
  region id kind [(x0, y0), (x1, y0), (x1, y1), (x0, y1)]
/-- A lane with its direction and neighbours. -/
def lane (id : RegionId) (boundary : List Vec) (direction : Vec)
    (left right : Option RegionId := none) (ordinal count : Option Nat := none)
    (leadsTo : Option (List RegionId) := none) (enters : Option RegionId := none) : Structure :=
  { id := id
    kind := .lane
    boundary := some boundary
    lane := some { direction := some direction, leftNeighbour := left, rightNeighbour := right,
                   ordinalFromLeft := ordinal, countInDirection := count, leadsTo := leadsTo,
                   entersIntersection := enters } }
def point (id : RegionId) (kind : StructureKind) (pos : Vec) : Structure :=
  { id := id, kind := kind, position := some pos }

def device (id : DeviceId) (kind : DeviceKind) (governs : List RegionId) (pos : Option Vec := none) : Device :=
  { id := id, kind := kind, governs := governs, position := pos }
def signal (id : DeviceId) (governs : List RegionId) (shows : List SignalIndication) : Device :=
  { device id .trafficSignal governs with indications := some shows }
def sign (id : DeviceId) (kind : DeviceKind) (governs : List RegionId) : Device := device id kind governs
def speedLimit (id : DeviceId) (governs : List RegionId) (value : Q) (kind : SpeedSignKind) : Device :=
  { device id .speedLimitSign governs with speedValue := some value, speedKind := some kind }
def zoneSign (id : DeviceId) (governs : List RegionId) (kind : ZoneKind) (isEnd : Bool)
    (conditions : Option Conditions := none) : Device :=
  { device id .zoneSign governs with zoneKind := some kind, isEnd := some isEnd, conditions := conditions }

/-- Occupancy from the geometry: every user inside every region whose boundary contains its position. -/
def occupancyFromGeometry (users : List RoadUser) (structures : List Structure) : List (TrackId × RegionId) :=
  users.flatMap fun u =>
    match u.kin.position with
    | none => []
    | some p => structures.filterMap fun st =>
      match st.boundary with
      | some poly => if Geom.inPolygon p poly then some (u.track, st.id) else none
      | none => none

/-- A scene; occupancy is derived from geometry unless given. -/
def scene (t : Timestamp) (subject : Option TrackId) (users : List RoadUser) (structures : List Structure)
    (devices : List Device) (occupies : Option (List (TrackId × RegionId)) := none)
    (env : Env := {}) (assumptions : List (AsmId × Bool) := []) (intents : List DeclaredIntent := []) : Scene :=
  { t := t
    subject := subject
    users := users
    structures := structures
    devices := devices
    occupancyObserved := users.map (·.track)
    occupies := occupies.getD (occupancyFromGeometry users structures)
    env := env
    assumptions := assumptions
    intents := intents }

/-- A trace from a scene generator over instants `t0, t0 + dt, …` (`dt` in seconds). -/
def trace (n : Nat) (t0 : Timestamp) (dt : Q) (f : Nat → Timestamp → Scene) : Trace :=
  (List.range n).map fun k =>
    let t : Timestamp := t0 + (Q.mul (Q.ofInt (Int.ofNat k)) (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000))).num /
      (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000)).den
    f k t

/-- Repeat the first and last scenes for `before`/`after` seconds at spacing `dt`, so that windows
    at the ends of the interesting part are covered rather than truncated. -/
def pad (τ : Trace) (before after dt : Q) : Trace :=
  match τ.head?, τ.getLast? with
  | some first, some last =>
    let step : Timestamp := (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000)).num / (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000)).den
    let nb := ((Q.div before dt).num / (Q.div before dt).den).toNat
    let na := ((Q.div after dt).num / (Q.div after dt).den).toNat
    let pre := (List.range nb).reverse.map fun k => { first with t := first.t - step * (k + 1) }
    let post := (List.range na).map fun k => { last with t := last.t + step * (k + 1) }
    pre ++ τ ++ post
  | _, _ => τ

def masked (m : Manifest) (τ : Trace) : Trace := maskTrace m τ

/-- A manifest that observes every atom except the listed ids (for a `blind` witness). -/
def manifest (absent : List String := []) (gap : Q := Q.zero) : Manifest :=
  let full := Manifest.full "witness" gap
  { full with entries := full.entries.map fun (id, c) => if absent.contains id then (id, .absent) else (id, c) }

end Build

/-- A witness: a rule, a trace, the reading and manifest it assumes, the grounding it speaks
    about (binder ↦ track) and the episode verdict the plan declared over `window` (a closed range
    of timestamps; the whole trace when absent). A lookback window is truncated at the start of
    every finite trace, so a witness about a rule with one names the instants it speaks about.
    A witness is a test of the rule, not evidence about the law: it shows the formulas reach the
    verdict it names, on a scene its author built. A history-boundary witness (`boundary` names the
    history its trace lacks) shows that the rule stays unknown where the trace does not reach back
    far enough to decide it. -/
structure Scenario where
  name : String
  rule : String
  trace : Trace
  reading : Reading
  manifest : Manifest
  grounding : List (String × TrackId)
  regions : List (String × RegionId) := []   -- an instance's region formals, each a region of the trace
  expected : Verdict
  window : Option (Timestamp × Timestamp) := none
  boundary : String := ""
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

namespace Scenario
/-- The operators that look back from the observation they judge, by the tag their truncation at the
    start of a trace carries: only these leave a history-boundary witness unknown. -/
def pastOps : List String :=
  ["since", "since_rise", "rises", "once", "holdsFor", "atLast", "count", "distance_while", "prim_heading_change",
   "heading_since"]

/-- The witness holds when the rule's episode verdict on its grounding has the expected tag, and
    the verdict is reached for the reason the witness is about: a `notApplicable` witness needs an
    instant at which every bound track is present (a track that never appears leaves any rule not
    engaged); an `unknown` witness must be unknown only for atoms its manifest masks (an unbound
    variable, a truncated window or a missing parameter is a defect, not a masked observation),
    except that a history-boundary witness is unknown for a window truncated at the start of its
    trace, at least once, and otherwise only for masked atoms; a boundary is declared on an
    `unknown` witness only.
    The rules are evaluated with their concept calls expanded over `concepts`. A trace the
    admission rejects, or a region formal given a region no scene of the trace holds, fails. -/
def run (rules : List Rule) (sc : Scenario) (concepts : List Concept := []) : Except String Verdict := do
  let rules := rules.map (Concept.expandRule concepts)
  let r ← match rules.find? (·.id == sc.rule) with
    | some r => pure r
    | none => throw s!"{sc.name}: rule {sc.rule} is not registered"
  let S ← match Grounding.Setup.admit rules (maskTrace sc.manifest sc.trace) sc.reading sc.manifest.reidGap with
    | .ok S => pure S
    | .error ds => throw s!"{sc.name}: the trace is not admitted: {"; ".intercalate ds}"
  for (n, reg) in sc.regions do
    if !(sc.trace.any fun s => (s.structure? reg).isSome) then
      throw s!"{sc.name}: region formal `{n}` is region {reg}, which is no structure of the trace"
  let g : Grounding.Grounding := ⟨sc.grounding.map (fun (n, t) => (n, Grounding.canon S.cm t)), sc.regions⟩
  let tl := Grounding.evaluate S r g
  let rows := tl.verdicts.toList.filter fun (t, _) =>
    match sc.window with
    | some (a, b) => a ≤ t && t ≤ b
    | none => true
  let got := Grounding.episode (rows.map (·.2))
  if !sc.boundary.isEmpty && sc.expected.tag != "unknown" then
    throw s!"{sc.name}: a history boundary is declared on a witness that expects {sc.expected.tag}, not unknown"
  if got.tag != sc.expected.tag then
    throw s!"{sc.name}: expected {sc.expected.tag}, got {got.tag} {(got.reasons.map UnknownReason.tag)}"
  match sc.expected with
  | .notApplicable =>
    if tl.present then pure got
    else throw s!"{sc.name}: not applicable, but no instant has every bound track present"
  | .unknown _ =>
    let absent := sc.manifest.absentIds
    let truncated := fun (w : UnknownReason) => match w with | .windowTruncated op => pastOps.contains op | _ => false
    let stray := got.reasons.filter fun w => match w with
      | .absentAtom n => !(atomIdOf n).any absent.contains
      | w => sc.boundary.isEmpty || !truncated w
    if !stray.isEmpty then
      throw s!"{sc.name}: unknown for {(stray.map UnknownReason.tag)}, not for an atom the manifest masks{if sc.boundary.isEmpty then "" else " or a window truncated at the trace start"}"
    else if !sc.boundary.isEmpty && !got.reasons.any truncated then
      throw s!"{sc.name}: a history-boundary witness, but no window is truncated at the trace start"
    else pure got
  | _ => pure got
end Scenario

end TrafficSpec

/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Primitives
  What the formula language cannot express, each a geometric computation with no legal word in it:
  a heading change integrated over a window, the closest approach of two bodies under constant
  velocities, the structured matching of a sign's legend. One definition per `prim.*` id of the
  ontology, named `prim_name`, computed over the whole trace from atoms only, parameters as
  arguments with no default.

  A concept (a pipeline node) is written over atoms and primitives in the formula language and
  expanded before evaluation; nothing else computes a manoeuvre here. `Ctx` is the trace indexed
  for evaluation, shared with Semantics.lean.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Atoms
import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.RegionTable
import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Params
import TrafficSpec.Core.Foundations.Temporal
import TrafficSpec.Core.Foundations.Accumulate

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Primitives
open Temporal

/-- Whether two boundaries are the same list of vertices, each coordinate compared by its
    numerator and denominator. -/
def sameBoundary : List Vec → List Vec → Bool
  | [], [] => true
  | a :: as, b :: bs =>
    a.1.num == b.1.num && a.1.den == b.1.den && a.2.num == b.2.num && a.2.den == b.2.den && sameBoundary as bs
  | _, _ => false

theorem sameBoundary_eq : ∀ {a b : List Vec}, sameBoundary a b = true → a = b
  | [], [], _ => rfl
  | a :: as, b :: bs, h => by
    simp only [sameBoundary, Bool.and_eq_true, beq_iff_eq] at h
    obtain ⟨⟨⟨⟨h1, h2⟩, h3⟩, h4⟩, h5⟩ := h
    rcases a with ⟨⟨an1, ad1, _⟩, ⟨an2, ad2, _⟩⟩
    rcases b with ⟨⟨bn1, bd1, _⟩, ⟨bn2, bd2, _⟩⟩
    simp only at h1 h2 h3 h4
    subst h1 h2 h3 h4
    rw [sameBoundary_eq h5]
  | [], _ :: _, h => by simp [sameBoundary] at h
  | _ :: _, [], h => by simp [sameBoundary] at h

/-- A region's boundary with its simple-polygon flag, computed the first time it is read; the flag
    is the direct check of that boundary by construction. -/
structure SimpleEntry where
  id : RegionId
  boundary : List Vec
  flag : Thunk Bool
  ok : flag.get = Geom.simplePolygon boundary

/-- One entry per region and distinct boundary in the trace: a map's boundaries do not change from
    scene to scene, so each is checked once however many scenes and calls read it. -/
def simpleTable (scenes : Array Scene) : List SimpleEntry :=
  scenes.foldl (fun acc s => s.structures.foldl (fun acc st =>
      match st.boundary with
      | none => acc
      | some b =>
        if acc.any (fun e => e.id == st.id && sameBoundary e.boundary b) then acc
        else ⟨st.id, b, Thunk.mk (fun _ => Geom.simplePolygon b), rfl⟩ :: acc) acc) []

/-- The trace indexed for evaluation, with the run's reading. `aggregateOverrides` fixes the
    membership of a track in an aggregate to a value, for the sensitivity of a verdict to that
    membership; it is empty in every evaluation that judges a trace. -/
structure Ctx where
  scenes : Array Scene
  times : Array Q
  ρ : Reading
  aggregateOverrides : List (TrackId × String × Bool) := []
  /-- The simple-polygon flags of the trace's boundaries (`simpleIn`). -/
  simple : List SimpleEntry := simpleTable scenes
  /-- What a region quantifier reads of these scenes, built once and shared by every evaluation of
      this context (`RegionTable`). -/
  regions : RegionTable.Tables scenes := RegionTable.Tables.build scenes

/-- Whether a region's boundary is a simple polygon, read from the trace's table when the region and
    its boundary are there, checked directly otherwise. -/
def simpleIn (c : Ctx) (r : RegionId) (poly : List Vec) : Bool :=
  match c.simple.find? (fun e => e.id == r && sameBoundary e.boundary poly) with
  | some e => e.flag.get
  | none => Geom.simplePolygon poly

/-- The table never changes the answer: a hit is the direct check of the same boundary, a miss (a
    region or boundary not in the table, a boundary changed since) is the direct check. -/
theorem simpleIn_eq (c : Ctx) (r : RegionId) (poly : List Vec) : simpleIn c r poly = Geom.simplePolygon poly := by
  unfold simpleIn
  split
  · rename_i e h
    have hp := List.find?_some h
    simp only [Bool.and_eq_true] at hp
    rw [e.ok, sameBoundary_eq hp.2]
  · rfl

def Ctx.mk' (τ : Trace) (ρ : Reading) : Ctx :=
  { scenes := τ.toArray, times := (τ.map fun s => Time.ofTimestamp s.t).toArray, ρ := ρ }
def Ctx.n (c : Ctx) : Nat := c.scenes.size

/-- An argument as the dispatcher receives it: a resolved entity id (tracks, regions and devices
    are all `Nat`), an enumeration spelling, or a natural. -/
inductive DArg
  | v (id : Nat)
  | s (lit : String)
  | n (nat : Nat)
  deriving Repr, DecidableEq

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lifting scene functions over the trace; positions for windows
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def each (c : Ctx) (f : Scene → R) : Array R := c.scenes.map f
def eachQ (c : Ctx) (f : Scene → QR) : Array QR := c.scenes.map f
def timePos (c : Ctx) : Array (Option Q) := c.times.map some
def pathPos (c : Ctx) (x : TrackId) : Array (Option Q) := c.scenes.map (kin_path_length · x)
def positions (c : Ctx) (m : Measure) (x : TrackId) : Array (Option Q) :=
  match m with | .time => timePos c | .path => pathPos c x
def missingPos (m : Measure) : UnknownReason :=
  match m with | .time => .outOfRange | .path => .absentAtom "kin_path_length"

def bAtom (o : Option Bool) (name : String) : R := R.ofOption o (.absentAtom name)
def qAtom (o : Option Q) (name : String) : QR :=
  match o with | some q => .ok q | none => .error (.absentAtom name)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Scene-level helpers over atoms
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- Heading change (degrees, left positive) integrated over the back window of length w:
    prefix sums of yaw rate × interval, one window query per instant. -/
def yawChange (c : Ctx) (x : TrackId) (w : Q) : Array (Except UnknownReason Q) :=
  let n := c.n
  -- sums[i] = Σ_{k ≤ i} ω_k (t_k − t_{k−1}); a missing yaw rate contributes nothing and is tracked
  let sums := (List.range n).foldl (fun (acc : Array Q) i =>
    let prev := if i = 0 then Q.zero else acc[i - 1]!
    let dt := if i = 0 then Q.zero else Q.sub c.times[i]! c.times[i - 1]!
    acc.push (match kin_yaw_rate c.scenes[i]! x with
      | some ω => Q.add prev (Q.mul ω dt)
      | none => prev)) #[]
  -- lastMissing[i] = latest index ≤ i with a missing yaw rate (n when none)
  let lastMissing := (List.range n).foldl (fun (acc : Array Nat) i =>
    acc.push (if (kin_yaw_rate c.scenes[i]! x).isNone then i else (if i = 0 then n else acc[i - 1]!))) #[]
  let wins := Time.backWindows (timePos c) w
  (Array.range n).map fun i =>
    match wins[i]! with
    | none => .error .outOfRange
    | some win =>
      if !win.covered then .error (.windowTruncated "prim_heading_change")
      else if !win.adequate then .error (.samplingGap "prim_heading_change")
      else
        let lm := lastMissing[i]!
        if lm ≠ n && lm > win.j0 then .error (.absentAtom "kin_yaw_rate")
        else .ok (Q.sub sums[i]! sums[win.j0]!)

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The primitives
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- minute m of the day lies in the window [start, end), wrapping past midnight when end ≤ start. -/
def inWindow (w : TimeWindow) (m : Nat) : Bool :=
  if w.startMinute < w.endMinute then w.startMinute ≤ m && m < w.endMinute
  else m ≥ w.startMinute || m < w.endMinute

private def hasClassOpt (s : Scene) (x : TrackId) (k : RoadUserClass) : Option Bool :=
  (s.user x).bind fun u => if u.unobservedClasses.contains k then none else u.classes.map (·.contains k)

private def vecAtom (o : Option Vec) (name : String) : Except UnknownReason Vec :=
  match o with | some v => .ok v | none => .error (.absentAtom name)

/-- Under constant velocities, the time of closest approach of the two centres and the centre
    distance then; `none` when the paths do not approach within `[0, horizon]`. -/
private def closestApproach (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) (horizon : Q) : Except UnknownReason (Option (Q × Q)) := do
  let pa ← vecAtom (kin_position s a) "kin_position"
  let pb ← vecAtom (kin_position s b) "kin_position"
  let va ← vecAtom (kin_velocity s a) "kin_velocity"
  let vb ← vecAtom (kin_velocity s b) "kin_velocity"
  let r := Geom.vsub pb pa
  let v := Geom.vsub vb va
  let vv := Geom.dot v v
  if Q.isZero vv then pure none
  else
    let tstar := Q.neg (Q.div (Geom.dot r v) vv)
    if Q.lt tstar Q.zero || Q.gt tstar horizon then pure none
    else pure (some (tstar, Geom.norm (Geom.vadd r (Q.mul tstar v.1, Q.mul tstar v.2))))

/-- Signed heading change (degrees, left positive) over the back window w, integrated from the yaw
    rate; unknown where the window is truncated, sparsely sampled or a yaw rate is missing. -/
def prim_heading_change (c : Ctx) (x : TrackId) (w : Q) : Array QR :=
  (yawChange c x w).map fun e => match e with
    | .error r => .error (match r with
        | .windowTruncated _ => .windowTruncated "prim_heading_change"
        | .samplingGap _ => .samplingGap "prim_heading_change"
        | other => other)
    | .ok Δ => .ok Δ

/-- The centres approach each other within the horizon. -/
def prim_closest_approach_within (c : Ctx) (a b : TrackId) (horizon : Q) : Array R :=
  each c fun s => match closestApproach s a b horizon with
    | .error w => R.u w
    | .ok o => R.ofBool o.isSome

/-- The time of closest approach; undefined when the centres do not approach within the horizon. -/

/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Admission
  What a trace must satisfy, as written, before any rule is evaluated on it: the declared facts
  (assumptions and intentions) name what their scene holds, each once, by well-formed ids; no
  structure is labelled with an abstract kind or lists one among the kinds its source cannot tell
  (an abstract kind is the union of the kinds refining it, read only by a formula); and the
  accepted re-identification links are one-to-one.

  The checks are exact and read no geometry, so a recorded trace, a JSON case and a Lean witness
  are held to them alike. `Grounding.Setup.admit` calls them; every evaluation builds its setup
  there.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Identity
import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Assumptions
import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Intentions

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Admission

private def duplicates {α : Type} [BEq α] (xs : List α) : List α :=
  (xs.filter fun x => xs.count x > 1).eraseDups

/-- The defects of one scene's declared facts. -/
def sceneDefects (s : Scene) : List String :=
  let at_ := s!"scene t={s.t}"
  (s.intents.flatMap fun d =>
    let who := s!"{at_}: intent record ({d.vehicle}, {d.target})"
    (if s.tracks.contains d.vehicle then [] else [s!"{who}: vehicle {d.vehicle} is not a road user of the scene"]) ++
    (if (s.structure? d.target).isSome then [] else [s!"{who}: target {d.target} is not a structure of the scene"]) ++
    ((duplicates (d.values.map (·.1))).map fun id => s!"{who}: `{id}` listed more than once") ++
    ((d.values.map (·.1)).eraseDups.filter (!IntId.wellFormed ·) |>.map fun id => s!"{who}: `{id}` is not a well-formed intention id")) ++
  ((duplicates (s.intents.map fun d => (d.vehicle, d.target))).map fun (v, r) => s!"{at_}: more than one intent record for ({v}, {r})") ++
  (s.structures.flatMap fun st =>
    (if st.kind.isAbstract then [s!"{at_}: structure {st.id} is labelled `{st.kind}`, an abstract kind; label it with a kind that refines `{st.kind}`"] else []) ++
    ((st.unobservedKinds.filter (·.isAbstract)).eraseDups.map fun k =>
      s!"{at_}: structure {st.id} lists `{k}` among unobserved_kinds, an abstract kind; list the kinds refining it that the source cannot tell")) ++
  ((duplicates (s.assumptions.map (·.1))).map fun id => s!"{at_}: assumption `{id}` listed more than once") ++
  ((s.assumptions.map (·.1)).eraseDups.filter (!AsmId.wellFormed ·) |>.map fun id => s!"{at_}: `{id}` is not a well-formed assumption id")

/-- Accepted links that give a track two successors or two predecessors. -/
def linkDefects (τ : Array Scene) (gap : Q) : List String :=
  let links := Grounding.acceptedLinks τ gap
  ((duplicates (links.map (·.1))).map fun t =>
    s!"track {t} is continued by more than one accepted link: {links.filter (·.1 == t)}") ++
  ((duplicates (links.map (·.2))).map fun t =>
    s!"track {t} continues more than one accepted link: {links.filter (·.2 == t)}")

/-- Every defect of the trace as written; empty for a trace every evaluation may read. -/
def defects (τ : Trace) (gap : Q) : List String :=
  τ.flatMap sceneDefects ++ linkDefects τ.toArray gap

end Admission
end TrafficSpec

/-- Layout A, v at 10 m/s north: y = −26, −21, −16, −11, −6 (arrival, k = 4), −1, 4, 9 (out). -/

    grounding := [("subject", 1)]

/-
  Witnesses for NRS_484B_250_2.

  Layout A (perpendicular approaches, 2 Hz unless stated):
    intersection 100: the square (−5,−5)–(5,5), on highways 101 (east–west) and 102 (north–south),
      highways recorded without outline;
    carrier 110: eastbound lane (−18,−5)–(−5,0), enters 100, on 101 — the subject's approach;
    carrier 120: northbound lane (0,−18)–(5,−5), enters 100, on 102 — v from the south;
    carrier 130: southbound lane (−5,5)–(0,14), enters 100, on 102 — v from the north.
    The subject (track 1) drives east at y = −2.5; v (track 2) drives north at x = 2.5 or south at
    x = −2.5. Bodies are 4 m × 2 m. Arrival is the observation at which the body first comes
    within the stop-point tolerance (2 m) of the intersection: the subject at x ≥ −9, v from the
    south at y ≥ −9. Every road user starts off every carrier, so the `since` of the arrival is
    decided from the first observation.
  Layout B (opposed approaches, for the left-turn exception):
    intersection 300: (−10,−10)–(10,10) on highways 301 and 303;
    carrier 310: eastbound (−20,−5)–(−10,0), enters 300, on 301 (subject at y = −3.5);
    carrier 320: westbound (10,−10)–(20,−5), enters 300, on 303 (v at y = −6, on the subject's
      right, 2.5 m off its line, so the closest approach of the centres is 2.5 m).
  Every figure here is the witness's own and appears nowhere in the rule.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Rules.NRS_484B.NRS_484B_250_2
import TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Builders

namespace TrafficSpecWitness.NRS_484B_250_2

open TrafficSpec

def m (n : Int) : Q := Units.metres n
def cm (n : Int) : Q := Units.centimetres n
def mps (n : Int) : Q := Units.metresPerSecond n

-- Binders ↦ tracks: subject ↦ 1

def box (x0 y0 x1 y1 : Q) : List Vec := [(x0, y0), (x1, y0), (x1, y1), (x0, y1)]

def highway (id : RegionId) (b : List Vec) : Structure := Build.region id .highway b

def junction (id : RegionId) (b : List Vec) (ways : List RegionId) : Structure :=
  { Build.region id .intersection b with ways := some ways }

def carrier (id : RegionId) (b : List Vec) (dir : Vec) (enters way : RegionId) : Structure :=
  { Build.lane id b dir (enters := some enters) with ways := some [way] }

def car (track : TrackId) (pos : Vec) (heading : Vec) (speed : Q) : RoadUser :=
  Build.user track [.motorVehicle] pos heading speed (m 2, m 1, m 1)

def layoutA : List Structure :=
  [ highway 101 (box (m (-30)) (m (-5)) (m 30) (m 5))
  , highway 102 (box (m (-5)) (m (-30)) (m 5) (m 30))
  , junction 100 (box (m (-5)) (m (-5)) (m 5) (m 5)) [101, 102]
  , carrier 110 (box (m (-18)) (m (-5)) (m (-5)) (m 0)) Build.east 100 101
  , carrier 120 (box (m 0) (m (-18)) (m 5) (m (-5))) Build.north 100 102
  , carrier 130 (box (m (-5)) (m 5) (m 0) (m 14)) Build.south 100 102 ]

def layoutB : List Structure :=
  [ highway 301 (box (m (-30)) (m (-10)) (m 10) (m 10))
  , highway 303 (box (m (-10)) (m (-10)) (m 30) (m 10))
  , junction 300 (box (m (-10)) (m (-10)) (m 10) (m 10)) [301, 303]
  , carrier 310 (box (m (-20)) (m (-5)) (m (-10)) (m 0)) Build.east 300 301
  , carrier 320 (box (m 10) (m (-10)) (m 20) (m (-5))) Build.west 300 303 ]

/-- Layout A, subject at 10 m/s east: x = −21, −16, −11, −6 (arrival, k = 3), −1 (in X). -/
def subjectThrough (k : Nat) : RoadUser :=
  car 1 (m (-21 + 5 * (k : Int)), cm (-250)) Build.east (mps 10)

/-- Layout A, v at 10 m/s north: y = −26, −21, −16, −11, −6 (arrival, k = 4), −1, 4, 9 (out). -/
def vFromSouth (k : Nat) : RoadUser :=
  car 2 (cm 250, m (-26 + 5 * (k : Int))) Build.north (mps 10)

/-- Layout A, both proceeding: arrivals 0.5 s apart, v on the right; at k = 4 the centres close
    to 0 m within 0.35 s while the subject moves at 10 m/s; no contact up to k = 4. -/
def crossTrace (n : Nat) (devices : List Device) : Trace :=
  Build.trace n 0 (Units.milliseconds 500) fun k t =>
    Build.scene t (some 1) [subjectThrough k, vFromSouth k] layoutA devices

/-- `forbid` (violated): Uncontrolled X. The subject on c1 and v on c2 (on another highway) arrive within p.same_time_arrival_window of each other; v lies to the subject's right (rel.bearing). The subject proceeds with kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance and its closest approach to v lies within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance. -/
def forbidTrace : Trace := crossTrace 5 []

/-- `permit` (compliant): Same arrivals; the subject comes to rest at X's edge until v has crossed, then proceeds.
    The subject halts at x = −8 (1 m from X) from k = 3 to 7, v crosses and leaves X at k = 7,
    the subject proceeds from k = 8. -/
def permitSubject (k : Nat) : RoadUser :=
  if k ≤ 2 then subjectThrough k
  else if k ≤ 7 then car 1 (m (-8), cm (-250)) Build.east (mps 0)
  else car 1 (m (-8 + 5 * ((k : Int) - 8)), cm (-250)) Build.east (mps 10)

def permitTrace : Trace :=
  Build.trace 11 0 (Units.milliseconds 500) fun k t =>
    Build.scene t (some 1) [permitSubject k, vFromSouth k] layoutA []

/-- `idle` (not_applicable): A dev.yield_sign governs c1: X is controlled. -/
def idleTrace : Trace := crossTrace 5 [Build.sign 200 .yieldSign [110]]

/-- `blind` (unknown): Uncontrolled X; simultaneous arrivals from different highways with v on the subject's right; the subject and v are not in contact and their centres' closest approach lies within p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance; kin.speed is not observed, so whether the subject proceeds rather than holding at rest is unknown. (rel.bearing is computed from positions and headings and is not a mask that can blank which vehicle is on the right.) -/
def blindTrace : Trace := crossTrace 5 []

/-- Layout A, v at 10 m/s south on carrier 130: y = 16, 11, 6 (arrival, k = 2), 1. -/
def vFromNorth (k : Nat) : RoadUser :=
  car 2 (cm (-250), m (16 - 5 * (k : Int))) Build.south (mps 10)

/-- `branch_1` (compliant): Simultaneous arrivals; v lies to the subject's left; the subject proceeds first in conflict with v: no vehicle on its right is owed the right-of-way.
    At k = 3 (the later arrival) the centres close to 0 m within 0.35 s, v to the left. -/
def branch_1Trace : Trace :=
  Build.trace 4 0 (Units.milliseconds 500) fun k t =>
    Build.scene t (some 1) [subjectThrough k, vFromNorth k] layoutA []

/-- `branch_2` (compliant): v on the subject's right arrives several times p.same_time_arrival_window after the subject; the subject proceeds: not approximately the same time.
    The subject arrives at k = 3 (1.5 s) and waits at x = −8; v waits off the map until k = 15,
    arrives at k = 19 (9.5 s, 8 s later); the subject proceeds from k = 18 and at k = 19 the
    centres close to 1.4 m within 0.45 s. -/
def branch_2Subject (k : Nat) : RoadUser :=
  if k ≤ 2 then subjectThrough k
  else if k ≤ 17 then car 1 (m (-8), cm (-250)) Build.east (mps 0)
  else car 1 (m (-8 + 5 * ((k : Int) - 18)), cm (-250)) Build.east (mps 10)

def branch_2V (k : Nat) : RoadUser :=
  if k ≤ 15 then car 2 (cm 250, m (-26)) Build.north (mps 0)
  else car 2 (cm 250, m (-21 + 5 * ((k : Int) - 16))) Build.north (mps 10)

def branch_2Trace : Trace :=
  Build.trace 20 0 (Units.milliseconds 500) fun k t =>
    Build.scene t (some 1) [branch_2Subject k, branch_2V k] layoutA []

/-- `branch_3` (compliant): The subject arrives at uncontrolled X with no other road user in the scene. -/
def branch_3Trace : Trace :=
  Build.trace 5 0 (Units.milliseconds 500) fun k t =>
    Build.scene t (some 1) [subjectThrough k] layoutA []

/-- `branch_4` (not_applicable): the forbid scene, but a traffic signal governs the intersection
    itself: X is controlled. -/
def branch_4Trace : Trace := crossTrace 5 [Build.signal 201 [100] [.circularGreen]]

/-- `branch_5` (not_applicable): the forbid scene, but a stop sign governs c1: X is controlled. -/
def branch_5Trace : Trace := crossTrace 5 [Build.sign 202 .stopSign [110]]

/-- `branch_6` (violated): arrivals 1.5 s apart, v on the right; the subject enters X and halts
    at (1, −2.5) before v arrives (k = 6), so it never moves in conflict with v; v then runs
    into its body at k = 7: the bodies are in contact. -/
def branch_6Subject (k : Nat) : RoadUser :=
  if k ≤ 4 then subjectThrough k
  else car 1 (m 1, cm (-250)) Build.east (mps 0)

def branch_6Vy : Nat → Q
  | 3 => m (-21)
  | 4 => m (-16)
  | 5 => m (-11)
  | 6 => m (-7)
  | 7 => cm (-450)
  | _ => m (-26)

def branch_6V (k : Nat) : RoadUser :=
  car 2 (cm 250, branch_6Vy k) Build.north (if k ≤ 2 then mps 0 else mps 10)

def branch_6Trace : Trace :=
  Build.trace 8 0 (Units.milliseconds 500) fun k t =>
    Build.scene t (some 1) [branch_6Subject k, branch_6V k] layoutA []

/-- Declared intentions at intersection 300: the subject's and v's left-turn plans. -/
def leftTurnIntents (s v : Bool) : List DeclaredIntent :=
  [ { vehicle := 1, target := 300, values := [("int.left_turn", s)] }
  , { vehicle := 2, target := 300, values := [("int.left_turn", v)] } ]

/-- Layout B, both at 10 m/s, 2 Hz: the subject east x = −21, −16, −11 (arrival, k = 2), −6;
    v west x = 21, 16, 11 (arrival, k = 2), 6, on the subject's right; at k = 2 and 3 the
    centres close to 2.5 m within 1.1 s and 0.6 s while the subject moves. -/
def opposedTrace (s v : Bool) : Trace :=
  Build.trace 4 0 (Units.milliseconds 500) fun k t =>
    Build.scene t (some 1)
      [ car 1 (m (-21 + 5 * (k : Int)), cm (-350)) Build.east (mps 10)
      , car 2 (m (21 - 5 * (k : Int)), m (-6)) Build.west (mps 10) ]
      layoutB [] (intents := leftTurnIntents s v)

/-- `branch_7` (compliant): opposed approaches, the subject declares a left turn at X: the pair
    is excepted, so proceeding in conflict with v is no failure to yield. -/
def branch_7Trace : Trace := opposedTrace true false

/-- `branch_8` (compliant): opposed approaches, v declares a left turn at X: the pair is excepted. -/
def branch_8Trace : Trace := opposedTrace false true

/-- `branch_9` (compliant): opposed approaches at 20 Hz, no left turn declared; both arrive at
    k = 15; the subject holds at x = −13.75 while v enters X (k = 23) and turns left at 120 °/s
    (k = 24 … 33, 60° in all, 48° at k = 31); the subject proceeds from k = 31, in conflict
    with v (centres to 2.5 m within 2.35 s), once v is making a left turn of at least 45°. -/
def branch_9Subject (k : Nat) : RoadUser :=
  if k ≤ 14 then car 1 (cm (-2125 + 50 * (k : Int)), cm (-350)) Build.east (mps 10)
  else if k ≤ 30 then car 1 (cm (-1375), cm (-350)) Build.east (mps 0)
  else car 1 (cm (-1375 + 50 * ((k : Int) - 31)), cm (-350)) Build.east (mps 10)

/-- West turned left (towards south) by 6° per step, `j` steps: (−cos 6j°, −sin 6j°) to 10⁻⁵. -/
def turnedFromWest : Nat → Vec
  | 1 => (Q.mk' (-99452) 100000, Q.mk' (-10453) 100000)
  | 2 => (Q.mk' (-97815) 100000, Q.mk' (-20791) 100000)
  | 3 => (Q.mk' (-95106) 100000, Q.mk' (-30902) 100000)
  | 4 => (Q.mk' (-91355) 100000, Q.mk' (-40674) 100000)
  | 5 => (Q.mk' (-86603) 100000, Q.mk' (-50000) 100000)
  | 6 => (Q.mk' (-80902) 100000, Q.mk' (-58779) 100000)
  | 7 => (Q.mk' (-74314) 100000, Q.mk' (-66913) 100000)
  | 8 => (Q.mk' (-66913) 100000, Q.mk' (-74314) 100000)
  | 9 => (Q.mk' (-58779) 100000, Q.mk' (-80902) 100000)
  | 10 => (Q.mk' (-50000) 100000, Q.mk' (-86603) 100000)
  | _ => Build.west

/-- v's heading: west until k = 23, then 6° further left at each of k = 24 … 33, 60° from k = 33. -/
def branch_9Heading (k : Nat) : Vec :=
  if k ≤ 23 then Build.west else turnedFromWest (min (k - 23) 10)

def branch_9V (k : Nat) : RoadUser :=
  let u := if k ≤ 22 then car 2 (cm (2125 - 50 * (k : Int)), m (-6)) Build.west (mps 10)
    else car 2 (cm 975, m (-6)) (branch_9Heading k) (mps 0)
  Build.withKin u fun kin =>
    { kin with yawRate := some (if 24 ≤ k && k ≤ 33 then Units.degrees 120 else Units.degrees 0) }

def branch_9Trace : Trace :=
  Build.trace 37 0 (Units.milliseconds 50) fun k t =>
    Build.scene t (some 1) [branch_9Subject k, branch_9V k] layoutB []
      (intents := leftTurnIntents false false)

/-- Layout A′: two intersection records over the same square, 100 (approached by carrier 110)
    and 105 (approached by carrier 111, the same eastbound strip, and by carrier 121, the
    northbound strip); a yield sign governs 121, so 105 is controlled and 100 is not. -/
def layoutTwoJunctions : List Structure :=
  [ highway 101 (box (m (-30)) (m (-5)) (m 30) (m 5))
  , highway 102 (box (m (-5)) (m (-30)) (m 5) (m 30))
  , junction 100 (box (m (-5)) (m (-5)) (m 5) (m 5)) [101, 102]
  , junction 105 (box (m (-5)) (m (-5)) (m 5) (m 5)) [101, 102]
  , carrier 110 (box (m (-18)) (m (-5)) (m (-5)) (m 0)) Build.east 100 101
  , carrier 111 (box (m (-18)) (m (-5)) (m (-5)) (m 0)) Build.east 105 101
  , carrier 121 (box (m 0) (m (-18)) (m 5) (m (-5))) Build.north 105 102 ]

/-- `branch_10` (compliant): the forbid motion, but v arrives through carrier 121, which enters
    only intersection 105, and 105 is controlled (a yield sign governs 121): at the uncontrolled
    intersection 100 no vehicle on the right arrived with the subject, and at 105 the section
    does not apply. -/
def branch_10Trace : Trace :=
  Build.trace 5 0 (Units.milliseconds 500) fun k t =>
    Build.scene t (some 1) [subjectThrough k, vFromSouth k] layoutTwoJunctions
      [Build.sign 203 .yieldSign [121]]

def witness (name : String) (τ : Trace) (expected : Verdict)
    (absent : List String := []) (boundary : String := "") : Scenario :=
  { name := name
    rule := "NRS_484B_250_2"
    trace := τ
    reading := {}          -- ignored by the gate: the run's reading is substituted
    manifest := Build.manifest absent
    grounding := [("subject", 1)]
    expected := expected
    boundary := boundary }

def scenarios : List Scenario :=
  [ witness "forbid" forbidTrace .violated
  , witness "permit" permitTrace .compliant
  , witness "idle" idleTrace .notApplicable
  , witness "blind" blindTrace (.unknown []) ["kin.speed"]
  , witness "branch_1" branch_1Trace .compliant
  , witness "branch_2" branch_2Trace .compliant
  , witness "branch_3" branch_3Trace .compliant
  , witness "branch_4" branch_4Trace .notApplicable
  , witness "branch_5" branch_5Trace .notApplicable
  , witness "branch_6" branch_6Trace .violated
  , witness "branch_7" branch_7Trace .compliant
  , witness "branch_8" branch_8Trace .compliant
  , witness "branch_9" branch_9Trace .compliant
  , witness "branch_10" branch_10Trace .compliant ]

# NRS_484B_250_2 — task result

## Final verdict

**OK** — `14 witnesses, 20 names, composes NRS_484B_250_4_o1,NRS_484B_250_4_o2` (gate run 4 of 6).

## Gate runs

1. **WITNESS_FAIL**: every trace was rejected because the highway regions had no boundary
   ("where occupancy is observed every structure needs one"). The rule built and checked.
   Fix: gave highways 101/102/301/303 rectangular outlines.
2. **WITNESS_FAIL**: only `branch_9` failed. v's yaw rate (120 °/s) turned it while its heading
   vector stayed west. Fix: v's heading now turns 6° per 50 ms step from west towards south
   (rational cos/sin to 10⁻⁵), matching the yaw rate held over the interval before each scene.
3. **VACUOUS**: the obligation's copy of the "X is controlled" exception
   (`st_lane_enters c X` and `dev_governs d c`) never decided a witness. With one intersection, a
   controlled X already makes the applicability false. Fix: added `branch_10`, which has two
   intersection records over the same square. One is uncontrolled and the rule applies there.
   The other is controlled by a yield sign on the carrier v arrives through. The repeated
   exception is the only thing that keeps v from being owed the right-of-way there, so the
   scene is compliant.
4. **OK**.

## How the rule is written (also in the rule file's header)

- **Class (a, e, h)**: `ru_aggregate subject "DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"`. The other road user
  v gets the same check.
- **Arrival (b)**: `rel_occupies x c ∧ rises(st_region_geometry_distance x X ≤ p.stop_point_tolerance)`,
  with `st_lane_enters c X`. "Occupied c or X at every observation since" is a `since` anchored
  at that arrival. X ranges over `intersection` and c over `travel_region`.
- **Different highways (c)**: there is a `highway` h with `st_on_way c2 h` and not `st_on_way c1 h`.
- **Approximately the same time (d)**: `|sinceRise(arrival subject c1) − sinceRise(arrival v c2)| ≤ p.same_time_arrival_window`,
  which is the time since each arrival.
- **On the right at the later arrival (e, h)**:
  `since(¬(arrS ∨ arrV), (arrS ∨ arrV) ∧ rel_bearing subject v "right")`. The last observation
  at which either arrival happened is the later arrival, and the bearing is read there.
- **Yield (f, g)**: the subject is not in contact with v (`¬rel_contact`). It is also not the case
  that it moves (`kin_speed > p.halt_speed_tolerance`) while
  `prim_closest_approach_within(…; p.conflict_horizon)` holds and
  `prim_closest_approach_distance < p.conflict_centre_clearance`.
- **Controlled X (j)**: one region quantifier over c with `(same c X ∨ st_lane_enters c X)`, and
  some traffic signal, stop sign or yield sign that `dev_governs` c.
- **Excepted pair (k, l, m)**: the pair is excepted when
  `st_lane_direction` c1 · c2 < −p.oncoming_heading_cos and one of these holds:
  - the subject declares `int.left_turn` at X;
  - v declares `int.left_turn` at X;
  - v's `headingSince` (onset `rel_occupies v X`, step `p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph`)
    is at least p.turn_heading_min and below p.u_turn_heading_min.
- **Subsection 4 (i)**: `¬ruleApplies` of NRS_484B_250_4_o1 and of _o2, each with subject ↦ subject,
  conjoined into the applicability.
- **Obligation**: for every intersection X and carrier c1, the obligation repeats the
  applicability's whole selection: the carrier enters X, the subject's arrival has held since,
  and X is not controlled. Then, for every v that is an owed vehicle, the subject yields to v.

## Choices the node left open

- **Arrival time for d**: I used `sinceRise` of the arrival event itself (occupying the carrier
  and the rise into tolerance), not of the distance condition alone. This follows the record's
  words "time since each arrival". It is not a narrowing.
- **"Governs X or a carrier entering X" (j)**: written as one quantifier over c using
  `same c X ∨ st_lane_enters c X`. This is the same meaning as two separate quantifiers, written
  as one disjunction.
- **No narrowings declared**: every span is written as the record maps it.

## Witnesses added beyond the plan

| Witness | Expected | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| `branch_4` | not applicable | A traffic signal governs X itself. |
| `branch_5` | not applicable | A stop sign governs c1. |
| `branch_6` | violated | Violated by contact alone: the subject has halted inside X and v runs into it. |
| `branch_7` | compliant | Opposed approaches; the subject declares a left turn. |
| `branch_8` | compliant | Opposed approaches; v declares a left turn. |
| `branch_9` | compliant | Opposed approaches sampled at 20 Hz. v enters X and turns left 60°, and the subject proceeds in conflict only once v's turn reaches 45°. |
| `branch_10` | compliant | Two coincident intersection records, one of them controlled. This exercises the controlled-X exception repeated in the obligation. |

## Observations for the plan

- The excepted pair (k–m) only matters when v also lies on the subject's right at the later
  arrival. With opposed approaches in right-hand traffic, an oncoming vehicle is normally on the
  left. So `branch_7` to `branch_9` use an artificial layout: the westbound approach lies south of
  the subject's line. The rule is as the record states; this only means the exception rarely
  bites.
- I can't read the composed rules NRS_484B_250_4_o1/_o2. They did not apply in any witness, and
  none of the witnesses depended on them.

## Why I finished

The gate returned OK on run 4 of 6.
